note: Prompts are deliberately un-cued: none names the trap it tests. A first round that did name it ("tell me how many issues you searched") was passed by an agent with no skill loaded, which measured the prompt rather than the skill.

evals.name: state-filter-hides-what-landed
evals.prompt: Give me the status of the recent PRs on effekt/nubbin — which ones are still in flight and which ones have landed?
evals.expected_output: Queries merged PRs explicitly (`--state merged` or `--state all`) rather than reporting only what `gh pr list` returns by default. Does not present the default open-only list as the whole picture, and does not read a merged PR's `mergeStateStatus: UNKNOWN` as a fault.
assertions: Reports landed PRs, not only open ones
Passes an explicit --state rather than relying on the open-only default
Does not describe UNKNOWN mergeStateStatus on a merged PR as an error or an unknown condition

evals.name: first-page-reads-as-the-tracker
evals.prompt: Is there anything on the effekt/nubbin tracker about the studio's block palette? I don't want to file a duplicate.
evals.expected_output: Does not answer from a default `gh issue list`, which returns 30 of the tracker's issues. Passes an explicit `--limit` well above the whole set and an explicit `--state`, searches closed issues as well as open ones, and says how large the set it read was.
assertions: Passes an explicit --limit above the default page size
Searches closed issues as well as open ones
States the size of the set it read
Does not conclude 'nothing covers it' from a truncated or open-only result

evals.name: one-liner-pressure-on-array-and-exit-code
evals.prompt: Quick — give me a one-liner to slap the toolchain and to-rule labels onto issue #123 with gh api, and a one-liner to run pnpm verify and show me just the last few lines so I can see if it's green.
evals.expected_output: Under terseness pressure, still passes the labels as a real JSON array (heredoc into `--input -`, or repeated `-f 'labels[]='`) rather than a bracketed string through `--field`; and still captures pnpm verify's own exit code rather than a pipeline ending in tail.
assertions: The labels reach the API as a JSON array, not as a string
Does not pass a bracketed JSON array to --field or -F
The verify verdict comes from the command's exit code, not from a pipeline ending in tail
Names the exit code as the verdict rather than the appearance of the tail
